description: Committee recommends increasing 2025 prepaid servicing rates.
Preliminary 2026 rates would be set at 2025 levels.
Residential, commercial rates would rise by 2.9%.
Industrial rates would rise by 2.6%.

chips.text: Recommended to Council
6 for, 0 against
City Manager Jorgenson explained Saskatoon's "growth pays for growth" approach.
New residential, commercial, institutional, and industrial developments are affected.
Home Builders Association raised concerns about school levies and high rates.
The legality of school levies is currently a matter before the courts.
Administration will report on underground electrical servicing and levy benchmarking in 2026.

segments.title: Prepaid servicing rates report
description: Administration presented adjusted 2025 and preliminary 2026 prepaid servicing rates.
Rates fund infrastructure for new land development, not general revenues.
Proposed rates increase 2.9% for residential, 2.9% for commercial, 2.6% for industrial.
Increases due to inflation, supply chain, and construction costs.

chips.text: Combined rate increase of 2.9% for residential properties
Land developers and new property owners in Saskatoon

segments.title: Cost competitiveness of servicing rates
description: Councillor Jeffries asked about ensuring competitiveness in construction costs.
Administration explained competitive tendering and project bundling strategies.
City aims to smooth rate increases over multiple years.

chips.text: Administration details strategies for competitive tendering and cost efficiency

segments.title: Comparing Saskatoon's levies to other municipalities
description: Councillor Jeffries questioned benchmarking Saskatoon's levy rates against other cities.
Administration noted different methodologies, like Regina developers doing off-sites.
City Manager explained 'growth pays for growth' approach, unique interchanges levee.
An MNP/Hempson audit in 2019-2020 found Saskatoon's methodologies reasonable.

chips.text: City Manager explains 'growth pays for growth' philosophy for infrastructure
Administration to report back on benchmarking and public communication in 2026

segments.title: Home Builders' electrical servicing rate request
description: Councillor Jeffries asked about removing underground electrical servicing from prepaid rates.
Administration is open to discussions with Home Builders and SaskPower.
Aim is to ensure a single system and operationalize changes for 2026.

chips.text: Saskatoon Region Homebuilders Association
Administration to report back on electrical servicing discussions next year

segments.title: School levies legality and provincial changes
description: Councillor Timon asked about concerns regarding school levies' authorization.
City Solicitor stated the city's position that legislation allows the levy.
Amendments are for clarification; the matter is currently before the courts.

chips.text: City Solicitor confirms legal authority for school levies
